SMTO-GWT-0074 — This GPU readings request asks for too much at once

GUID: 88c18cde-83f6-5b8b-88e2-85906c795b7d
Slug: gpu-sample-limit-exceeded
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO takes repeated GPU readings for at most 5 minutes and 120 readings at a time, spaced 0.5 to 60 seconds apart. This request went past those limits, so no readings were taken.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again with a smaller request: readings every 0.5 to 60 seconds, no more than 120 readings, and no longer than 5 minutes in total. These are the fixed limits for one set of GPU readings.
  2. Only ask for readings SMTO offers: usage, memory used, total and percent, temperature, power use and power limit. A request for any other measurement is refused before readings start.
  3. To watch a GPU for longer than 5 minutes, ask SMTO to set up a monitor instead. Monitors are SMTO's way to keep watching over time; GPU readings are only for short checks.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the set of GPU readings you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't split a long watch into many back-to-back reading requests; use a monitor instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The gpu.sample request violated its schema or sampling bounds (interval 0.5-60 s, at most 120 samples, total span at most 300 s, unique valid GPU UUIDs, documented fields only).

What this means

  • Sampling violated its typed schema or its interval, device/field selection, sample count or total-duration bounds. The category is not limited to a long duration. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Sampling violated its typed schema or its interval, device/field selection, sample count or total-duration bounds. The category is not limited to a long duration.

How to diagnose it

  • Check schema detail, 0.5–60 second interval, at most 120 samples and at most 300 seconds, including valid unique fields and UUIDs.

How to fix it

  • Resubmit gpu.sample with interval_seconds between 0.5 and 60 and exactly one of samples (<= 120) or duration_seconds (<= 300, giving floor(duration / interval) + 1 <= 120 samples), keeping (samples - 1) x interval <= 300 s; use only the documented fields and unique GPU-... UUIDs. Use the Monitor skill for longer observation.
  • Correct the sampling fields and bounds; use Monitor for a longer watch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use 0.5-60 second intervals, at most 120 samples and at most 300 seconds. Use Monitor for longer work.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid bounded sample completes with its requested fields; longer observation uses the existing Monitor workflow.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
